FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: artichokes à la barigoule
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: small violet artichokes turned and split, sweated in {1_plur} with a mirepoix, moistened with white {2_plur} and left to reduce dry. The name comes from a mushroom nobody has put in for two centuries.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: artichokes vinaigrette
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} boiled whole and head down, served warm with a mustard vinaigrette. You pull the leaves off one by one and scrape the base of each between your teeth; the heart is kept for last.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: stuffed artichokes
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cleared of their choke, filled with a {1_adj} stuffing bound with crumb, and braised upright in a little stock until the leaves open of their own accord.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: carciofi alla romana
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} trimmed down to the tender heart, stuffed with {1_plur} and Roman mint, planted stem upwards in a narrow pan and sweated in oil and water.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: carciofi alla giudia
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} whole fried twice over, crushed between the two fryings so that the leaves open into a flower and turn as brittle as crisps. An invention of the Roman ghetto.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: risotto ai carciofi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} pearled and moistened ladle by ladle, {0_coll} cut into slivers and added in two goes — the first at the start to melt away, the rest at the end to stay firm — then bound with {2_plur}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pasta ai carciofi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} shaved fine and melted down in {2_plur} and oil, let down with a little cooking water to bind the pasta without cream.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: frittata di carciofi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} fried until they gild, drowned in {1_plur} beaten with {2_plur}, cooked over a very low flame then turned over with a plate. Eaten cold, cut into wedges.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: parmigiana di carciofi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} sliced, floured and fried, built up in layers with {1_plur} and {2_plur}, then browned. Less known than the aubergine version, and finer.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: artichoke pizza
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} marinated in oil and laid on the base at the last moment, with {2_coll} — one of the four quarters of a capricciosa, promoted to a whole dish.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: alcachofas con jamón
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} blanched and then fried in {2_plur} with {1_plur} cut into dice, which gives up its fat and salts the dish without anything else being added.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: aginares a la polita
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised in oil with {1_coll} and carrots, bound with an {2_adj} avgolemono mounted off the heat. In the manner of the City — meaning Constantinople.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: zeytinyağlı enginar
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the bottoms of {0_adj} filled with {2_plur} and diced carrot, cooked in {1_adj} oil and cooled in it. Turkish olive-oil dishes are always eaten cold.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: dolma qarnoun
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the bottoms of {0_adj} filled with a hash of {1_adj} and {2_adj}, stewed in a white lemon sauce. The Algerian dish of spring, when the cardoons come in.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: artichoke tagine
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} stewed with saffron and ginger, {0_coll} added halfway through so as not to fall apart, and preserved {2_coll} at the very end.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: spinach and artichoke dip
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} chopped and drowned in melted {2_plur}, browned and served boiling with something to dip. The American party dish above all others, and nobody stops in time.
